text: Later a man appeared on the beach. <break time="0.8s" /> And began waving his coat. <break time="0.8s" /> And soon a hotel bus full of people. <break time="0.8s" /> Stopped to watch the boat. <break time="0.8s" /> The men hoped for a rescue. <break time="0.8s" /> But the people on shore only waved. <break time="0.8s" /> As if they thought. <break time="0.8s" /> The boat was out fishing. <break time="0.8s" /> Darkness came on at last. <break time="0.8s" /> The man and the bus disappearing. <break time="0.8s" /> And the four men were alone again. <break time="0.8s" /> With the cold sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the long night. <break time="0.8s" /> The oiler and the correspondent rowed in turns. <break time="0.8s" /> While the cook talked about pies. <break time="0.8s" /> Until he fell asleep. <break time="0.8s" /> The water was so cold. <break time="0.8s" /> That the sleeping men. <break time="0.8s" /> In the bottom of the boat. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay shivering. <break time="0.8s" /> Their legs tangled together. <break time="0.8s" /> Once, while the others slept. <break time="0.8s" /> A great fin cut through the dark water. <break time="0.8s" /> Near the boat. <break time="0.8s" /> Leaving a trail of blue light. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent felt. <break time="0.8s" /> As if he were the only man. <break time="0.8s" /> On all the oceans. <break time="0.8s" /> And he wished. <break time="0.8s" /> That a friend would wake up. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he remembered a poem. <break time="0.8s" /> From his school days. <break time="0.8s" /> About a soldier of the Legion. <break time="0.8s" /> Who lay dying in Algiers. <break time="0.8s" /> Far from his home. <break time="0.8s" /> As a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> He had never cared about that soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> But now, cold and alone at sea. <break time="0.8s" /> He felt the mans sorrow. <break time="0.8s" /> As his own.
